subject: factor levels implicitly reordered when subsetting data

messages.author: 4f9701b3dc2dae8c
messages.subject: factor levels implicitly reordered when subsetting data
parts:
Hi,

In 0.90, I'm applying different geoms to different subsets of the
data. When I plot all data together in g1, the factor level ordering
is preserved. However, when I plot subsets in g2, the ordering isn't
preserved. Any idea how to fix this?

Thanks,
Gad


d <- data.frame(
X=rnorm(30),
Y=rnorm(30),
Z=sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 30, TRUE)
)

levels(d$Z) <- c("C", "B", "A")

g <- ggplot(d, aes(x=X, y=Y, colour=Z, size=Z))

# order preserved
g1 <- g + geom_point()

# levels get reordered
g2 <- g + geom_point(data=d[d$Z != "A", ])
g2 <- g2 + geom_point(data=d[d$Z == "A", ])

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: factor levels implicitly reordered when subsetting data
parts:
On Wed, May 2, 2012 at 5:46 PM, Gad Abraham <gad.a...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> In 0.90, I'm applying different geoms to different subsets of the
> data. When I plot all data together in g1, the factor level ordering
> is preserved. However, when I plot subsets in g2, the ordering isn't
> preserved. Any idea how to fix this?
>
> Thanks,
> Gad
>
>
> d <- data.frame(
>   X=rnorm(30),
>   Y=rnorm(30),
>   Z=sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 30, TRUE)
> )
>
> levels(d$Z) <- c("C", "B", "A")
>
> g <- ggplot(d, aes(x=X, y=Y, colour=Z, size=Z))
>
> # order preserved
> g1 <- g + geom_point()
>
> # levels get reordered
> g2 <- g + geom_point(data=d[d$Z != "A", ])

When I plot this, the levels rendered in the legend are C and B; since
the data from A are missing, the A level is silently dropped when the
legend is trained.

Although the factor levels of Z are consistent throughout the data
(sub)sets, your second call to g2 above is adding a new layer to the
existing ggplot object g2, whose legend has silently dropped the A
level. At this point, the legend has to be retrained to accommodate
the new subset, so the default behavior is probably to order
lexicographically. The workaround is to use scale_manual() on each
aesthetic:

g2 + scale_colour_manual(breaks = levels(d$Z), values = c('red',
'blue', 'black')) +
scale_size_manual(breaks = levels(d$Z), values = c(5, 3, 1))

HTH,
Dennis
